transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Aisha (NexusHealth CTO), Diego (Lead ML Eng), Samir (Infra)
Shared artifacts referenced: /drive/poc/benchmarks.xlsx, https://redwood.ai/poc/notes (internal), NexusHealth staging access doc (sent)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining our weekly sync. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:07] Diego: Diego on the line.
[00:09] Samir: Samir.
[00:11] Lucas: Lucas from Redwood.
[00:13] Maya: Great, quick agenda - review INT8 and FP8 runs from last week, look at quality deltas, discuss staging VPC runs, and agree next steps.

[01:02] Lucas: Ok so I pulled together the runs - INT8 baseline and FP8 experimental. For context we ran on the 4xA100-ish shape in our Dedicated cluster and then replicated a subset on your staging GCP VMs. INT8 results: memory down ~2x, throughput up ~1.6-1.9x depending on batch, tail latency improved ~15-25% on avg.

[01:40] Diego: When you say throughput up 1.9x is that tokens/sec for our 1k prompt distribution or for micro-batch?

[01:44] Lucas: Good question, that's observed tokens/sec in our end-to-end harness with a 1k median prompt length we used. For shorter prompts the delta is slightly lower, ~1.6x.

[02:20] Aisha: And quality? We measured a few thing internally - we care about hallucination rate and certain clinical QA checks.

[02:27] Lucas: Right. For INT8 we looked at automatic metrics plus a small sampled human eval. The overall automatic metrics (perplexity-ish proxy and an exact-match QA pass) were within ~0.5-1% of FP16 baseline. Human eval pass-rate from our small set dropped from 92% to 91% - noisy but within margin.

[03:05] Diego: Ok that sounds acceptable if it's in that band. What about FP8?

[03:09] Lucas: FP8 gives a bigger perf bump - we saw up to ~2.1-2.3x throughput in best cases, memory down further. But quality regressed more on long-tail prompts: our sampled human eval pass-rate dropped to ~89-90%, and a couple of edge QA cases failed where numeric precision mattered. So it's a tradeoff.

[03:46] Maya: To be clear: INT8 is safer with predictable small quality delta; FP8 is higher risk but higher reward on perf/cost.

[04:02] Samir: From infra perspective, FP8 also required a different kernel set and a small comp library tweak - are those supported in our on-prem image? We run a slightly old CUDA stack.

[04:11] Lucas: Good point. FP8 needs the newer kernel path; we flagged in the notes that on older drivers you hit fallback paths and lose perf. We'll include a compatibility matrix in the doc.

[04:40] Diego: One result I noticed in your sheet - the INT8 calibration step seemed sensitive to dynamic range. There was that run where the tail latency spiked. Can you explain?

[04:49] Lucas: Yeah that was the run where we used a static calibration without per-layer clipping. Switching to per-layer dynamic range reduces those spikes but adds a bit to calibration time. We can automate calibration during warmup to keep it transparent.

[05:15] Aisha: On the quality side, how are you measuring changes? We're especially worried about clinical instruction following for critical prompts.

[05:22] Lucas: We used a combination: automatic proxies (token-level perplexity proxy, exact-match on structured QA outputs) and a human pass/fail rubric for the 50-sample set you gave earlier. But that set wasn't representative of your 200-edge cases. Hence request for your larger prompt set.

[05:50] Diego: We'll push that set by end of week.

[06:05] Maya: Great. On the perf front, Samir, you mentioned network constraints for staging VPC runs?

[06:12] Samir: Yes, NexusHealth staging VPC has egress rules and a NAT gateway that's a bottleneck. We should do the perf run inside the VPC with instances hitting the Dedicated seats directly or use our private deployment flow.

[06:25] Lucas: We can run the harness inside your VPC; we'll need staging credentials and a short list of IPs. Also note we'll run two scenarios: cold start (no KV cache) and warmed-up KV cache to show real app-like latencies.

[07:00] Diego: Can you include traces? Flame graphs, and token breakdowns?

[07:04] Lucas: Yep - we'll attach traces and token-level latency histograms. The spreadsheet already has per-run CSVs; I'll add flame graphs.

[07:30] Aisha: Pricing - how much difference if we enable FP8 on Dedicated?

[07:35] Maya: Early numbers: FP8 can cut per-token infra cost by ~25-35% depending on batch and utilization. But there's an enablement fee and we typically recommend a pilot to validate quality. I'll follow up with a short pricing delta doc.

[08:05] Diego: Are there competitors doing FP8 at scale? I know some folks at Mosaic and Anthropic pushing mixed precision.

[08:12] Lucas: Yes, others are experimenting. Our differentiator is the eval + rollback tooling and the ability to route to safer variants automatically if quality dips. We can set up fallback policies so critical prompts always go to FP16 or a pinned model.

[08:45] Maya: Quick demo - Lucas, can you show the sheet highlights?

[08:50] Lucas: Sure. (screen share noises) Ok row 23 shows our INT8 run with per-layer calibration: 1.75x throughput, 18% median latency improvement, QA pass delta -0.9%. Row 47 is FP8: 2.2x throughput, 28% latency improvement, QA pass delta -2.8% on our sampled set, with two numeric edge failures noted.

[09:40] Diego: The -2.8% is a bit scary for clinical cases. We need human eval on our 200 prompts before considering FP8 for production.

[09:50] Lucas: Agreed. For FP8 we suggest a canary: route 5% of traffic to FP8 behind monitoring and automatic fallback if your quality metrics cross thresholds.

[10:20] Samir: Also confirm RBAC and audit logs for the pilot - we need SSO and k/v audit.

[10:27] Maya: Yep, we support SAML SSO, RBAC and audit logs at token-level. We'll share the security pack next.

[11:00] Aisha: Ok can we recap action items?

[11:05] Maya: Sure - Lucas will run the INT8 re-calibration with dynamic per-layer ranges and push updated CSVs and flame graphs (due 2026-03-12). Diego will upload the 200 prompt eval set and acceptance criteria (due 2026-03-14). Maya will send pricing delta and pilot SoW (due 2026-03-13). We'll schedule the VPC staging run once Samir provides IPs and access.

[11:35] Diego: One more thing - how do you handle model rollbacks if we see regression after canary?

[11:40] Lucas: We have an automatic rollback policy in the console. You can set thresholds on any metric (QA pass-rate, latency, error rate) and the router will failover to FP16/pinned variant. We can demo that in the next call.

[12:05] Aisha: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

[12:09] Maya: Thanks all, we'll send notes and the updated sheet. Meet same time next week.

(occasional crosstalk and short filler words omitted)

End of transcript.
